issues.legal_issue: A reviewing court should not disturb concurrent factual findings rejecting an alleged family partition when the findings were reached after examining the evidence.
material_facts: The landholders claimed that the family had separated and partitioned its land in two stages.
The Deputy Collector and Revenue Tribunal both rejected that claim after considering the evidence, including mutation intimations, land sales, affidavits, and records concerning agricultural produce.
The matter came before the Supreme Court in an appeal by special leave.
issues.conclusion: The Court declined to interfere with the concurrent finding that the alleged severance and partition had not been established.
issues.legal_principle: In an appeal under Article 136 of the Constitution, the Court would not be justified in interfering with a concurrent finding of fact reached after examination of the material. No earlier case was relied on for this issue.

predicates.special_leave_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal brought by special leave.
predicates.concurrent_factual_findings: The lower decision-makers reached the same factual finding.
predicates.findings_based_on_examined_evidence: The lower decision-makers reached that finding after examining the evidence placed before them.
predicates.concurrent_factual_finding_not_disturbed: The concurrent factual finding is left undisturbed.

issues.definition: When an appeal by special leave challenges a factual finding shared by the lower decision-makers and based on their examination of the evidence, that finding is left undisturbed.

issues.legal_issue: A family's ceiling holding is determined by its membership on the appointed day and does not fluctuate with later changes in membership, except where the statutory scheme provides for redetermination.
material_facts: The ceiling proceedings concerned a family holding agricultural land under the applicable ceiling legislation.
Three children were born into the family after the appointed day.
The Revenue Tribunal did not count those children when fixing the family's ceiling area.
issues.conclusion: The Tribunal correctly excluded the children born after the appointed day when determining the family's ceiling area.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 2(4), 3 and 4 establish the appointed day and provide for the ceiling to be imposed and determined by reference to that day; sections 8 and 9 regulate transfers and acquisitions on or after that day. Section 12 provides for reassessment in specified circumstances, but not merely because family membership later changes. The Court relied on State v. Dinkarrao Narayanrao Deshmukh (1969) 72 Bom. L.R. 237, Murari Rao S. Gube Patil v. State, Spl. C.A. No. 767 of 1968, and Spl. C.A. No. 229 of 1968, and held the contrary view in Civil Application No. 1578 of 1969 to be incorrect.

predicates.ceiling_determination_proceeding: The proceeding determines the ceiling holding of a person or family under an agricultural land ceiling scheme.
predicates.family_membership_changed_after_referenc: The number of family members changed after the day used to determine the ceiling holding.
predicates.no_statutory_redetermination_event: No specified event requiring the ceiling holding to be reassessed occurred.
predicates.ceiling_area_remains_based_on_reference_: The ceiling area remains based on the family's membership on the reference day.

issues.definition: If a ceiling determination involves a later change in family membership but no event requiring reassessment, the ceiling area remains based on membership on the reference day.

issues.legal_issue: A family member who holds land separately is excluded when calculating the family's additional ceiling allowance, but land acquired in that member's name is treated as family land, and the member is counted, when there is no evidence it was held separately.
material_facts: A family member had acquired land in his own name before the appointed day.
The Tribunal found no evidence that the land had been purchased from his separate funds or treated by him or the family as his separate property.
The Tribunal included the land in the family's holding and counted the member in calculating the family's additional ceiling allowance.
issues.conclusion: The Tribunal correctly treated the land as family property, counted the member, and allowed the corresponding additional ceiling area.
issues.legal_principle: Under the proviso to section 6 of the Maharashtra Agricultural Lands (Ceiling on Holdings) Act, 1961, a member who holds land separately is not regarded as a family member for the purpose of increasing the family's holding beyond the basic ceiling. If the land is treated as family property, it is included in the family's holding and the member is counted for the additional allowance. The Court relied on section 6 and its proviso.

predicates.family_ceiling_determination: The proceeding determines a family's ceiling holding and any additional allowance based on its membership.
predicates.land_acquired_in_member_name: Land was acquired in the name of a member of the family.
predicates.no_evidence_land_held_separately: There is no evidence that the member or family treated the land as the member's separate property.
predicates.land_counted_as_family_property_and_memb: The land is counted as family property and the member is counted in calculating the family's additional allowance.

issues.definition: When land acquired in a family member's name is not shown to have been held separately, it is counted as family property and that member is counted for the family's additional allowance.
